note: Opening clause verbatim; bracketed continuation is a summary rendering. A blog also lists 'Charity is selfishness.'

text: The belief in reincarnation will only help us to look the other side.
You have to liberate yourself.
We are not created for any grander purpose than the ants that are there or the flies that are hovering around you or the mosquitoes that are sucking your blood.
note: Wikisource ch.4 wording ('you'); aggregators give 'We are not created… than the ants… the flies… the mosquitoes' in third person. Supersedes the fragment entry above.

text: Each cell of a living organism cooperates with the cell next to it. … The cells stick together not out of brotherhood, love and that kind of thing, but out of the urgent drive to survive.
book: Society: It's terror, not love that keeps us together
note: Sunita Pant Bansal (ed.), foreword Mahesh Bhatt; passage closes with a line about destroying a neighbour. Goodreads work 45622919.

text: It is not love, compassion, humanism, or brotherly sentiments that will save mankind. It is the sheer terror of extinction that can save us, if anything can.
note: The Mind Is a Myth introduction samples the same idea as 'mutual terror, not love, will save mankind'; the Bansal anthology title renders it 'It's terror, not love that keeps us together'.

text: Our basic human problems are neurological, not psychological. Thought has created the problem of desire.
book: Certainty: Life has no beginning, no end
note: Search-summary paraphrase of Goodreads work 46398939 (Bansal anthology 'Certainty'); same page: drop the idea of the meaningful and you find meaning in daily life.

text: I have nothing to say and what I am saying is not born out of my thinking.
note: Transcribed conversation reproduced in Mahesh Bhatt's biography (blog serialisation); no date or venue given, so not confirmed as the 1972 Bangalore 'First and Last Public Talk'.

text: India will *not* be that country.
note: UG predicts the world crisis will produce its rescue from the West, grounding it in having spent half his life in the West.

text: …anything you superimpose on that, all the cultural input, is responsible for the boredom of man.
note: Quotepark 'Culture' tag; same page paraphrases 'as a human being I am rotten because of the culture'.

text: You draw lines on this planet.
note: Context: thought creates the world and its borders, so unity between countries is unreachable.

text: Hope is necessary for tomorrow, not for today.
note: Goodreads attribution; page formatting messy.

text: The peace you seek is already there; the effort to be at peace is what destroys it.
note: Paraphrase of the libquotes 'peace' topic passage.

text: Human nature is basically violent because thought itself is violent.
note: Hindu-blog collection; same page says the body dissolves into its elements at death and in that sense is immortal.

text: I have never taken any medicine or seen a doctor, except once for typhoid. I would never tell others not to see a doctor, though I say doctors should be shot.
note: Paraphrase from the Medium/WELL copies of the Swan Song.

text: I have one thing against medical technology…
note: Dated 1982 on quotewise/quotepark; continues about controlling the human being.

text: The body knows what it needs to survive; if it lacks the means it goes gracefully.
note: Recurs in inner-quest 'UG Words', hindu-blog and the Swan Song.

text: You need not worry about nutrition or health foods; the body turns whatever you put into it into energy.
note: Interview account in the 'UG Cookbook' PDF (travelswithug.com), at age 84; not verbatim.

text: …I knew without doubt that I had made the biggest mistake of my life.
note: On the morning after his arranged wedding; the same source reports he did not trust anyone who had not raised children to educate them ('if you raised your own children, you would understand').

text: If you could have sex with your own mother without any psychological or spiritual problem, that would be the end of your sexual desire.
note: Paraphrase of a Wikisource ch.8 dialogue; same passage: 'Thought always interferes with sex.'

text: There is no such thing as your mind and my mind. … mind is everywhere, sort of like the air we breathe.
People call me enlightened, a term I dislike; there is no such thing as enlightenment.
note: Summary paraphrase of a Wikiquote Mystique entry.

text: Charity is selfishness.
note: Blog list of sayings, source unclear.

text: Meditation is evil.
note: Fragment in Mark Whitwell's Medium essay; surrounding context cut off.

text: You are not a "person", not a "thing", not a discrete entity surrounded by "other" things.
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything

text: Your beliefs are the result of blind acceptance of authority, all secondhand stuff.
chapter: Ch. I The Certainty That Blasts Everything

text: is not yours; it is something which you and your ancestors have accumulated over a long time
chapter: Ch. III Not Knowing Is Your Natural State
note: Said of the knowledge a person holds.

text: belief is an extension of the survival mechanism which has operated for millions of years
chapter: Ch. III Not Knowing Is Your Natural State

text: My teaching, if that is the word you want to use, has no copyright.
note: Front-matter disclaimer reproduced in Mind is a Myth, No Way Out and other books.

text: We have invented reality. Otherwise you have no way of experiencing the reality of anything.
The basic question which we have to ask for ourselves is: what kind of a human being do you want? But unfortunately we have placed before ourselves the model of a perfect being.
note: Wikisource shows this wording in Chapter 8; Chapter 4 has the same question in other words.

text: That any fool can do, but the courage to be on your own, to stand on your two solid feet, is something which cannot be given by somebody.
chapter: Part III Nice Meeting You, and Goodbye
note: Preceded by: 'You can have the courage to climb the mountain, swim the lakes, go on a raft to the other side of the Atlantic or Pacific...'

text: My body had gone away and it has never come back. The points of contact are all that is there for the body.
Anything you touch is always translated as hard, soft, warm, cold, wet, dry and so on.
in the 'natural state' the continuity of thought is absent. What is present is a disjoined series of independent interactions.
the hands and feet become cold, the body becomes stiff, the heartbeat slows down
note: Describing the periodic death-like state of the body.

text: I am not against the scientific method per se.
note: Surfaced in a Wikisource dialogue; exact book not shown in search summary.

text: man, who supposedly has achieved so much progress in the scientific field, cannot even predict precisely when an earthquake is going to occur
I call it 'calamity' because from the point of view of one who thinks this is something fantastic, blissful and full of beatitude, love, or ecstasy, this is physical torture.
note: Describing the 1967 event; quoted in the WELL biography chapter 9.

text: Not a calamity to me but a calamity to those who have an image that something marvelous is going to happen.
The pleasure of sex, for instance, is by nature temporary.
wherever there is division, there can't be love
Love, compassion, ahimsa, understanding, bliss, all these things which religion and psychology have placed before man, are only adding to the strain of the body.
what you call sexual activity, which is biological in its nature, has been turned into a pleasure movement
the only test for me is money
the body does not know that it is healthy or unhealthy
nothing of what we consider to be good for the body is actually good for this body
You are trying to enforce peace through violence. Yoga, meditation, prayers, mantras, are all violent techniques.
All your experiences, all your meditations, all your prayer, all that you do, is self-centred.
The body cannot be afraid of death.
note: Opens a longer Goodreads quote: 'The body cannot be afraid of death. The movement that...'

text: in that sense the body is immortal
note: From a passage on clinical death and the body's constituent elements, quoted in the WELL memorial page.

text: The understanding that there is nothing to understand is all there is.
chapter: Ch. V We Have Created This Jungle Society

text: There is nothing to understand — that is the understanding I am talking about.
anything that is born out of thought is destructive in its nature
chapter: Ch. 3 What Is the Meaning of Life?
note: Chapter 6 (Seeking Strengthens Separation) has the variant 'any action that is born out of thinking is destructive in its nature'.

text: there is no entity called 'self' independent of the thought process
chapter: Ch. 1 The Unrational Philosophy of U.G. Krishnamurti

text: You don't have to do a thing.
chapter: Part I You Don't Have to Do a Thing
note: Title line of Part I; variant on inner-quest: 'to be yourself is very easy, you don't have to do a thing'.

text: thought is a divisive and ultimately a destructive instrument. It can only function in terms of a division between the so-called self or ego and the world.
note: WELL page summarising U.G.; may be editor's wording.

text: It [thought] is a mechanical thing and can solve only mechanical problems.
Time and space, apart from the ideas of 'time' and 'space', do not exist at all.
Thought is you.
I am only interested in describing this state, in clearing away the occultation and mystification in which those people in the 'holy business' have shrouded the whole thing.
It is a business; it has become a holy business to people.
It is fear that makes you believe that you are living and that you will be dead.
note: Aggregators cite Mystique of Enlightenment p.83 (Sentient ed.); some cite No Way Out.

text: Man created God out of fear; so the problem is fear, not God.
note: Wording varies by aggregator; quotepark cites Mind is a Myth.

text: there is no power outside of man
man has created religion because it gives him a cover
it is the ones who believe in God, who preach peace and talk of love, who have created the human jungle
It would be more interesting to learn from children, than try to teach them how to behave, how to live and how to function.
Because you cannot face the impermanence of all relationships, you invent sentiments, romance, and dramatic emotions to give them certainty.
I awoke the morning after my wedding night and knew without doubt that I had made the biggest mistake of my life.
note: Quoted in Mahesh Bhatt's biography (WELL ugbio4).

text: I am not anti-rational, just unrational. You may infer a rational meaning in what I say or do, but it is your doing, not mine.
chapter: Ch. 1 The Unrational Philosophy of U.G. Krishnamurti
note: Wikiquote cites No Way Out; Dharmapedia cites Stopped in Our Tracks.

text: Neither the subject nor the author is famous.
note: U.G.'s reaction to the idea of the book, recorded in the publisher's note.

text: I am neither a jivanmukta nor an evolved being.
chapter: Book One (Stories of U.G. in India)
note: Kwize excerpts: U.G. repeatedly denies being a liberated soul or an evolved being.

text: I have nothing to give; you have nothing to take.
What I am saying is outside the field of teachability; it is simply a description of the way I am functioning.
note: Search summary rendered in third person; wording close to the Wikisource text.

text: I had seven years of sadhana.
note: Autobiographical: between fourteen and twenty-one he visited Sivananda often and did austerities.

text: my grandfather knew Blavatsky and Olcott, and then, later on, the second and third generation of Theosophists
each individual has now the responsibility; not any particular nation — India or America or Russia
it has to come, and it will come from the West
note: Followed by the claim that India has no chance of being the source.

text: the idea of selflessness is a protective invention against one's actual selfishness
chapter: Ch. IV There Is Nothing to Understand
note: Summary of the chapter's opening answer.

text: the very birth of thought creates fear
chapter: Ch. V We Have Created This Jungle Society

text: Transformation, moksha, liberation, and all that stuff are just variations on the same theme: permanent happiness.
happiness without one moment of unhappiness, pleasure without pain, it is the same thing
note: Said of moksha/liberation/transformation.

text: There is no happiness.
note: Answer to a question about the secret of total happiness (inner-quest interview).

text: That is to say, all that is born out of thought is destructive, irrespective of its nature, whether it be religious, scientific or political.
The body or organism is not interested in spiritual matters.
This can also lead to self-destruction for the sake of even a silly idea, as witnessed in wars.
The body changes from one state into another as recycling of matter.
note: Wikisource text; preceded by 'So also are the birth and death of thought.'

text: Political institutions and ideologies are the warty outgrowth of the religious thinking of the man; in a way responsible for the tragedy of mankind.
Yes it is. Because thought is violent. Anything that is born out of thought is destructive.
note: Answer to a question whether thought is violent (holybooks PDF of the book).

text: Don't forget that in the name of "Love thy neighbor as thyself" millions and millions of people have died, more than in all the recent wars put together.
The body does not exist except as a thought.
all we can know is memory and memory is thought
The natural state is not a thoughtless state; that is a hoax that has been carried on for thousands of years. You will never be without thought.
note: Search summary renders in indirect speech; the Wikisource text carries this claim.

text: The knowledge about it, all that he has learned, is held in the background, unless there is a demand.
note: Third-person description of the natural state quoted on Jhana 8.

text: It is a physiological state, with no religious or mystical content.
I am not suggesting that you should stop thinking; thought is what you are.
note: Rendered indirectly in the search summary of well.com/chandra.htm.

text: it is through this constant thinking that we are maintaining the continuity of what we call the 'I' or 'self'
note: WELL page paraphrasing U.G.

text: I don't exercise; I used to walk a great deal.
note: Reply to a questioner noting he does no yoga or exercises.

text: Making love is war.
All doctors should be shot.
note: Said he never took medicine or saw a doctor except once for typhoid; did not advise others against doctors.

text: modern day doctors are the modern day witches, and modern day medical technology the modern day witchcraft
eat what you like because the perfect intelligence of life knows exactly what to do with food
note: As recalled by Mark Whitwell.

text: the fear of losing what we have and what we know is responsible for our problems
note: Aggregators attribute variously to Mystique of Enlightenment and No Way Out.

text: I wasted seven years listening to him.
note: Biographical accounts of his break with J. Krishnamurti; wording not confirmed. Not a J. Krishnamurti quote.

text: a useless exercise
note: How U.G. later described his seven years of yoga and meditation with Swami Sivananda.
